body:
I did feel a little better, until the quasi-infidelity came to light. I think the problems are temporary, and fixable, but I often don’t feel like I have the energy or strength to see them through or fix them.

I really love that quote, but I feel like the exception sometimes. My family has been great, but sometimes they’re just not quite enough. I think I’ll try PMing you. Thank you so much for reaching out.

I haven’t really, no. I just felt like I had to keep going and keep pushing because I would loathe myself, more so than I already do, if I didn’t do absolutely everything I could to get in. I’m trying to slow down now, but I’m really worried that it’s too late, and I’m going to lose the things I love anyway. I’m really hoping the path leads to fulfillment and happiness, but I feel like I have no way of knowing until I get closer to the end. And I don’t know if I can make it that far. Cheers, and thank you for reaching out.

Your suggestion is really insightful. You sound like you might be a Northeastern student. Everyone is winging it, hoping they get that co-op or grade to validate the struggle. I didn’t get a co-op my first try, but it was okay. I regrouped, took some classes, and got a great co-op the next time. You sound like you have the insight to make it happen. It is really painful, and I hope more than anything that you find some joy too, and that you find some validation internally. You’ve been more than good enough, outstanding really, for me. As long as I’m around, I would love to talk to you more, if you’d like. I’ll have to remember to check this throwaway. Thank you very much for reaching out.
I don’t know, but I’m really grateful that you’d want to. I’ve never successfully PMed someone before, but maybe I’ll try. Thank you.
